what: life8 round-8 many-world search r8a, launched with the fixed code (critic B1, B2, F1, F2; see docs/life8/README.md 'Critic fixes before the cluster search').
status_at_handoff: running on all 4 hosts in tmux session life8-search. Every host was writing results.jsonl rows (17:02 UTC: adler40 1103, knecht24 637, specht32 359, falke64 683 round-0 rows). knecht24 finished round 0 in 28.6 min, kept 230 of 920 and started round 1 (1000 ticks) at 17:10 UTC; the others were due to finish round 0 at about 17:15-17:17 UTC.
launch_command: bash scripts/life8_search.sh start r8a 0 "--preset living --source bridged --rounds 4 --ticks 500 --growth 2 --keep 0.25 --reps 6 --branch-ticks 200 --perm-reps 100" adler40:22:1800:4000 knecht24:22:920:1500 specht32:10:620:3000 falke64:10:1100:3000
launch_environment: LIFE8_PLAN_WORKERS=24 (local world7 scan for the plan: 70 min on the shared Windows machine, seeds 0-12121 scanned)

plan.source: bridged: world7 worlds that reach bodies (bridge.candidate_worlds from seed 0) and synthetic planets (bridge.synthetic_world), alternating
plan.preset: living (config.LIVING: blooms, 0-3 predators from the planet via bridge.connect_ecology, calls beyond sight with their own gene, kin credit 1.0 attributed to the call (F1), receiver and reciprocity features, evolving genome); population_limit 256, compact log
plan.staged_locally: runs/life8-search/r8a/stage/plan.json and <host>.plan.json (git-ignored; split with python -m haishool.life8.search split)

shape.paired_branches: rounds 1-3, kept worlds only: 6 replicates x 200 ticks in 4 arms (normal, masked, scrambled, tools_off), world RNG reseeded identically per replicate
shape.measurement_window: last half of each round's segment
shape.criteria: search.CRITERIA; sender = within-sender excess >= 0.05 bits, p <= 0.01, and in paired rounds normal minus masked within-sender excess >= 0.02 bits; convention = situation-specific difference (F2)

hosts.cap_note: hard cap for the small disk; peak use expected about 0.6 GB in round 0 (0.6 MB per pending end state)

cost_measurement.bench_tag: r8-bench (tmux session life8-bench, finished; folder ~/life8-search/r8-bench kept, about 4 MB per host)
cost_measurement.bench_command: LIFE8_SESSION=life8-bench bash scripts/life8_search.sh start r8-bench 50000 "--preset living --source bridged --rounds 2 --ticks 300 --keep 0.5 --reps 2 --branch-ticks 100 --perm-reps 100" adler40:22:22:3000 knecht24:22:22:1500 specht32:10:10:3000 falke64:10:10:3000

bench_branch_wall.adler40: 72 branch tasks of 100 ticks in 15 s

cost_measurement.model: hours = round 0 (measured) + 1.3 x round-0 cost per tick x (segments of rounds 1-3 + 4 arms x 6 reps x 200 branch ticks per kept world) / workers, + about 0.2 h for tails and the main process

expected_finish.range_utc: 19:45-21:30 UTC (21:45-23:30 Berlin); populations of kept worlds set the later rounds' cost

commands.status: bash scripts/life8_search.sh status r8a adler40 knecht24 specht32 falke64
commands.watch_one_host: ssh -t adler40 tmux attach -t life8-search   (detach with Ctrl-b d; never Ctrl-c)
commands.collect: bash scripts/life8_search.sh collect r8a adler40 knecht24 specht32 falke64
commands.stop: bash scripts/life8_search.sh stop r8a HOST   (kills only the life8-search tmux session; the folder stays)
commands.resume: bash scripts/life8_search.sh resume r8a "--preset living --rounds 4 --ticks 500 --growth 2 --keep 0.25 --reps 6 --branch-ticks 200 --perm-reps 100" HOST:WORKERS:0:CAP_MB   (skips finished rounds and worlds; a new CAP_MB replaces the saved cap)

done_when: status shows 'tmux life8-search: none', 'complete rounds_done' from out/search.json and an 'exit 0' line at the end of search.log on every host
collect_and_report: 1. Run status; when a host shows stopped output_cap (only plausible on knecht24), resume it with a larger cap, e.g. knecht24:22:0:2500.

2. Run collect: it copies results.jsonl, search.json and search.log of each host to runs/life8-search/r8a/HOST/ and writes runs/life8-search/r8a/merged/report.json (per round: worlds, errors, stops, score median and max, passed criteria, language verdicts, kept; best final-round worlds) and summary.txt.

3. Report per round the counts of passed criteria next to the number of worlds x alpha (F3 is still open: there is no multiple-comparison guard). Chance passes to expect: the sender criterion needs p <= 0.01 (at most 1 in 100 worlds per round by chance), the fitness criterion needs 6 of 6 positive replicates (1 in 64 paired worlds by chance).

4. For the best final-round worlds (merged report 'best'), copy their checkpoints (~/life8-search/r8a/out/checkpoints/<id>.r3.json.gz on the host in the row's 'host' field) with scp and confirm locally on fresh replicate salts and held-out seeds before any claim; lineage.mapping_persistence needs numpy (local or knecht24) and a lineage table, which the bundle does not carry (critic F7).
5. Toy-world numbers: a passed criterion is a measured dependency or paired effect in this simulation, not language, technology or institutions.
6. After collecting, the host folders can be removed (ssh HOST rm -rf ~/life8-search/r8a ~/life8-search/r8-bench); nothing else was created on the hosts.
notes: Each host is exact with itself (resume on the same host); hosts are independent samples, not bit-identical reruns (critic F4: libm differences).
Disk at 16:52 UTC: adler40 42 GB free, knecht24 31 GB, specht32 222 GB, falke64 823 GB; round-0 pending end states take about 0.6 MB per world until selection.
No GPU, service, other folder or other tmux session on the hosts was touched; the searches run under nice 10 with 22/22/10/10 workers (2 hardware threads left free per host).

Tests at launch: python -m pytest tests/life8 -q gave 268 passed, 7 skipped; the slow founder test (test_experiments, -m slow) fails only its P(eat) margin, 0.5921 vs 0.5945 needed (unchanged, as instructed).
known_issue: 24 of the 4440 planned worlds (synthetic planets at exactly 273 K: adler40 9, knecht24 4, specht32 5, falke64 6) end with an error row 'temperature outside allowed range' in round 0: bridge.connect_ecology sets ambient_temperature = -0.15 C, objects cool below the thermal model's zero (0 C) and materials validation refuses them. Pre-existing ecology-stage bug, not in the critic's list; the rows are kept as errors and those worlds cannot continue (0.5% of the plan). Not fixed in the running code; fix: clip the connected ambient temperature (or the cooling target) at 0 C.
